content:
A clip from a year ago resurfaced on Monday—in which David Letterman slammed network executives for clearing late-night TV of Trump critics and shared his thoughts on the phenomenon—following the president's ban on White House press access.

The late-night legend opened his remarks at the Atlantic Festival 2025 by warning that under authoritarian governments and dictatorships, “sooner or later, everyone gets it.”

Letterman pointed to CBS's decision to cancel The Late Show hosted by his successor Stephen Colbert, blaming Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison for not wanting to “piss off” Trump.

He then noted ABC's suspension of Jimmy Kimmel's show after pro-Trump TV czar Brendan Carr threatened the network and its affiliate stations to take action against Kimmel over comments he made about the assassination of Charlie Kirk—which drew fire from the right.

“We're all seeing where this is going, right? This is the manipulated media,” Letterman said.

“It's not good. It's silly and it's stupid. You can't fire somebody because you're afraid of or trying to appease an authoritarian, criminal administration in the Oval Office. There's no place for that.”

The clip resurfaced on social media thanks to a post from former Labor Secretary Robert Reich.

“David Letterman's warning to the media from just a year ago sounds no less trenchant and no less sad today,” he wrote in the post.

“He was right: You cannot appease a tyrant.”
